hero.subtitle: Authorization Code Exchange for web and mobile — Amazon Developer Console setup, API reference, and frontend examples.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: Amazon login is optional and controlled by AMAZON_AUTH_ENABLED. When disabled, Amazon endpoints return 503 Service Unavailable. JWTs are never placed in the redirect URL; the API issues a one-time exchangeCode (Redis, 60 seconds). The same POST /auth/exchange endpoint is shared with other social providers.
items: Profile fetched via GET https://api.amazon.com/user/profile after token exchange
Scope profile for profile and email
Same token response shape as POST /auth/login

console.title: Amazon Developer Console (Login with Amazon)
console.description: Create a Security Profile under Login with Amazon at https://developer.amazon.com/. Add Allowed Return URLs matching AMAZON_CALLBACK_URL. Scope: profile.
steps: Open Amazon Developer Console → Login with Amazon
Create a Security Profile and note Client ID / Client Secret
Ensure AMAZON_CALLBACK_URL matches the Allowed Return URL
Request the profile scope during authorization

env.title: Environment variables
env.description: Loaded from .env via src/config/amazon-oauth.config.ts (namespace amazonOAuth on ConfigService). See .env.example.

roles.title: Default roles for new Amazon users
roles.description: New Amazon users receive roles: [] by default (same as password register). Set AMAZON_OAUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES in .env to a comma-separated list of Role values (e.g. user or user,manager). Existing users linked by email keep their current roles.

flow.title: Sequence
items: User consents on Amazon; browser hits GET /api/v1/auth/amazon/callback
API calls https://api.amazon.com/user/profile, upserts user, stores exchangeCode in Redis, redirects to redirect?code=...
Client POSTs { code } to /api/v1/auth/exchange and receives JWTs

start.title: 1. Start OAuth
start.description: Opens Amazon consent at https://www.amazon.com/ap/oa. Query redirect must match a prefix in AMAZON_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST (or omit to use the first allowlist entry). Scope: profile.

callback.title: 2. Callback
callback.description: Handled by the API. Token exchange uses https://api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token. Redirects to your app with ?code= (or &code= if the URL already has a query).

exchange.title: 3. Exchange code
exchange.description: Public endpoint shared with other social providers. Consumes the code (single use) and returns the same shape as login.

web.title: Frontend — Web (SPA)
web.description: Typical flow: button starts OAuth in the same window (or popup); a callback route on your frontend origin reads code from the query string and calls exchange.
notes: Add your frontend callback URL to AMAZON_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST (e.g. http://localhost:5173/auth/callback)
AMAZON_CALLBACK_URL must point at the Nest API, not the SPA
Store accessToken / refreshToken securely (memory + httpOnly cookie patterns as you prefer)

mobile.title: Frontend — Mobile (deep link)
mobile.description: Use a custom scheme (or universal link) in the allowlist. After Amazon, the API redirects to myapp://success?code=.... The app opens, parses the code, and calls exchange.
notes: Register the scheme in the OS / Expo app.json
Exchange over HTTPS against your API base URL

security.title: Security notes
items: Redirect URLs must match AMAZON_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST prefixes
Exchange codes are single-use and expire in 60 seconds (Redis)
Existing local users are linked by verified Amazon email (amazonId set; roles unchanged)
Amazon-only users have password null — password login / change-password will fail until a password is set
Email is required from https://api.amazon.com/user/profile; login fails if Amazon does not return an email

userModel.title: User model
userModel.description: Postgres entity / interface fields used by Amazon login:
items: amazonId — unique nullable Amazon user id
isActive — set true for new Amazon users
